Senses.Explanation: To hold fast is to keep something firmly in hand or under control. Chan records characteristically load the verb against ‘release or let go’ (放行): the two can name opposed exercises of authority, yet Wansong also says each can operate inside the other, so neither word fixes one outcome by itself. The compound has 684 occurrences in 186 allowlisted texts, and the contiguous pair ‘hold fast and release’ (把定放行) occurs 15 times in 13 texts. Wansong quotes the saying, ‘when held fast, true gold loses its color; when released, rubble shines’ (把定真金失色，放行瓦礫生光), and calls this ‘having capture and release, able to kill and bring to life’ (謂之有擒有縱，能殺能活). Xuedou preserves the same opposition: ‘when released, rubble shines; when held fast, true gold loses color; the authority is in hand, killing and bringing to life accord with the occasion’ (放行則瓦礫生光，把定則真金失色，權柄在手，殺活臨時). These lines contrast true gold and rubble under holding and release; they do not by themselves define gold as enlightenment or establish one symbolism for gold elsewhere. The common objects show the physical pressure retained by the verb: ‘hold heaven and earth fast’ (把定乾坤) has 113 occurrences in 60 texts; ‘hold the world fast’ (把定世界) 39 in 31; ‘hold the key crossing’ (把定要津) 29 in 22; and ‘hold the throat’ (把定咽喉) 8 in 8. Hongzhi calls ‘holding the throat’ the work of a good hand in commenting on an exchange. In a recorded question, Jiufeng is asked ‘what is the eye that holds heaven and earth fast?’ (如何是把定乾坤眼) and answers, ‘heaven and earth are inside it’ (乾坤在裏許), then identifies that as the heaven-and-earth eye (正是乾坤眼). Wansong elsewhere says one eye ‘is also called the eye that holds heaven and earth fast, continuously leaking not the slightest thread, and is also named the diamond eye at the crown’ (一隻眼又喚作把定乾坤眼，綿綿不漏絲毫，亦名頂門具金剛眼).
Senses.Note: The corpus uses the same verb for concrete grasping, for holding a passage or throat, and in the paired critical vocabulary ‘hold fast / release’ (把定／放行); these uses retain the literal opposition and do not require separate senses. Wansong further states, ‘where the ancients held fast, they could release and advance from the top of a pole; when releasing, they could hold firm, standing like a thousand-fathom wall’ (古人把定處放得行竿頭進步，放行時把得定壁立千仞). The record thus refuses a simple equation of holding with one fixed outcome; this entry reports the wording without assigning an intent to it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 裂開也在我，揑聚也在我。諸方道：把定真金失色，放行瓦礫生光。謂之有擒有縱，能殺能活。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong Xingxiu, in Wansong's Commentary on Tiantong's Old Cases and Further Inquiries (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚拈古請益錄), quotes the saying that true gold loses color when held and rubble shines when released, then names the pair capture/release and killing/bringing to life.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一隻眼又喚作把定乾坤眼，綿綿不漏絲毫，亦名頂門具金剛眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong Xingxiu, in Wansong's Commentary on Tiantong's Old Cases and Further Inquiries (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚拈古請益錄), says that one eye is called both the eye that holds heaven and earth fast and the diamond eye at the crown.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問九峯。如何是把定乾坤眼。峯云。乾坤在裏許。僧云。乾坤眼何在。峯云。正是乾坤眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Book of Serenity (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚頌古從容庵錄), Jiufeng Daoqian exchange: the questioning monk asks about the eye that holds heaven and earth fast, and Jiufeng answers that heaven and earth are inside it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 放行則瓦礫生光。把定則真金失色。權柄在手。殺活臨時。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Chan Master Mingjue (明覺禪師語錄), Xuedou Chongxian's own formal address: Xuedou says that rubble shines when released, true gold loses color when held, and authority kills or brings to life according to the occasion.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古人把定處放得行竿頭進步。放行時把得定壁立千仞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Book of Serenity (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚頌古從容庵錄), Wansong Xingxiu's prose on case 79: Wansong says that the ancients could release where they held fast and hold firm when releasing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乾坤把定不把定。虛空放行不放行。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Jiangshan Fang's formal address: Jiangshan asks whether heaven and earth are held fast or not, pairing the question with whether empty space is released or not.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。者僧解問。青林解弄。可謂是虛玄不犯。回互旁參。把定咽喉。方為好手。觸他毒氣。不是作家。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi (宏智禪師廣錄), Hongzhi Zhengjue's comment on the preceding exchange: Hongzhi says that holding the throat marks a good hand, while touching the other's poisonous energy does not mark an adept.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師拈起拄杖云。把定世界不漏絲髮。還觀得也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Chan Master Mingjue (明覺禪師語錄), Xuedou Chongxian's formal address: Xuedou raises his staff and says that holding the world fast does not leak a hair's breadth, then asks whether the assembly sees it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無門曰。一人向深深海底。行簸土揚塵。一人於高高山頂。立白浪滔天。把定放行各出一隻手。扶竪宗乘。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Gateless Barrier (無門關), Wumen Huikai's comment on the Qianfeng case: Wumen says that holding fast and releasing each put out one hand to uphold the lineage vehicle.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所以雪竇尋常道。威音王已前無師自悟。是第二句。還我第一句來。若未能把定要津。不免奔馳南北。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Chan Master Mingjue (明覺禪師語錄), Xuedou Chongxian's formal address: Xuedou says that one who cannot hold the key crossing fast cannot avoid running north and south.
